title: HarvestManifest
$comment: HAND-WRITTEN, and deliberately not in contracts/schemas/ — everything there is GENERATED from contracts/src by gen.ts, and every one of them is an MQTT wire payload. This is a file sidecar for a Python harvester with no bus surface. It moves into contracts the day a SECOND producer, in another language, writes one. PLAN-314.01.
description: Where one harvested file came from, written by the tool that fetched it, at the moment it fetched it. A manifest records a FETCH, not a file: a derivative (the Markdown rendering of a page, a summary PDF) carries no manifest of its own and names its source's instead.

source_url.description: The absolute URL fetched, query and fragment included if they were sent. This is the field the whole file exists for: The trees already in `scrapes/` predate manifests and encode it in the DIRECTORY PATH, which is why 3,245 tracked paths under `scrapes/microphones*/` contain `|` or `+` (git ls-files, 2026-10-30) and CLAUDE.md §1 calls them unsafe to touch. Encoding a URL as a path is what a manifest exists to stop.

retrieved_at.description: UTC, ISO 8601, Z-suffixed. When the fetch returned — not when the document was authored, and not when the file was last written.

http_status.description: The status of the response that produced this file. Null only where the record is reconstructed and the status is unknowable.

content_type.description: The Content-Type header as received. What the server SAID it was, which is not always what the extension claims.

content_length.description: Bytes written to disk. Compared against sha256 by the checker: a length that matches a stale digest is a file edited in place.

sha256.description: Of the bytes on disk. This is what makes 'is this the same document as that one' answerable — the question the AES 60 corpus could not answer, which left four pairs of genuinely different drafts labelled 'Duplicate Copy'.

fetcher.description: What wrote this. `Scraper.py` is the only one today; `browser` is the honest value for the AES 60 corpus, whose ' (1)' suffixes are a browser's duplicate-download naming and not a tool's.

provenance.description: `fetched` means every field above was observed at fetch time. `reconstructed` means a human backfilled it afterwards and at least one field is inference. A backfilled row that looks identical to a fetched one is worse than no row, so the distinction is a required part of the record rather than a comment.
provenance.$comment: Absent means `fetched` only for files written by a fetcher. A backfill MUST state it.

note.description: Free text for what the fields cannot carry — which of two near-identical drafts this is, why a status is null.
